title: Evidence
description: A record of something observed, attached to the assertion it bears on. Cross-cutting rather than owned by a stage (#25), so it carries no x-stage. Consumes #82's primitives and introduces none. ⚠️ Evidence does NOT carry a verdict or a confidence rung — it carries what was observed, and #96's derivation reads those observations. An evidence record that already knew the answer would make the derivation decorative.

allOf.$comment: Kind determines what must be present. Nested inside allOf per #82 — a top-level `if` beside allOf:[$ref] drops the envelope's evaluated-property annotations.

then.$comment: An experiment with no environment cannot be judged applicable to anything, which is what #96's filtering step needs above all else.

else.$comment: A source-based record must say where it came from, or it is an opinion with a citation field.

kind.description: Where the observation came from. `source`: authoritative documentation or published material. `experiment`: something was executed and observed. These reach different confidence rungs (#42) and are filtered for applicability differently (#96), so the distinction is structural rather than descriptive.

summary.description: What was observed, in one or two lines. Human orientation; the derivation does not read it.

sources.description: Where a `source` record came from. Structured because REQ-0004 requires a claim taken from a source to record that source, and a URL inside prose is not a record of anything.

environment.description: What the experiment ran in. REQ-0006 requires this in enough detail to judge whether it resembles the target, and #96's applicability filter is what does that judging. ⚠️ RESHAPED 2026-08-22 (#131) after two fixtures pressured it: `tier` used to be required alongside `facts`, which made a run executed directly on the host UNRECORDABLE — there was no honest value for it. The fix is two axes rather than a 'tier 0': every experiment declares an environment, and only a controller-managed run declares a sandboxTier.

execution.description: WHO ran it. `host`: executed directly, with whatever the machine had. `controller`: the validation controller provisioned an environment and ran it there. This is the discriminator that makes an absent sandboxTier meaningful rather than merely missing.

sandboxTier.description: #56's sandbox tier. Caps the reachable rung. ⚠️ Present ONLY when a controller supplied the isolation. A host run has no tier — not the lowest tier, NO tier: a rung implies a comparison, and 'isolation is not a thing this run has an answer to' is not the bottom of a ladder.

isolationBoundary.description: What the tier did and did not claim, travelling WITH the record (DEC-0005). A reader of this evidence must be able to see that tier 1 is not containment without going to find the decision that said so.

facts.description: Observed environment facts — os, kernel, interpreter, image, instance type, whatever the claim turns on. Compared against the assertion's targetEnvironment to decide applicability and environment match. Free-form keys on purpose: the dimensions that matter differ per claim, and a fixed list would be wrong for most of them.

omissions.description: Facts the observer does NOT have, each with why (#122, DEC-0005). ⚠️ These describe the OBSERVER, never relevance: whether a missing fact matters to a claim is decided per claim by the applicability layer (#123, #105). ⚠️ Unrequested facts stay simply absent — this array is for facts that were wanted and are not here, which is what makes an omission DETECTABLE rather than silent.

fact.description: The key this would have been, had it been collected.

state.description: not-captured: collection was deliberately disabled, or no collector was running. not-observable: the requested fact has no available collector. unavailable: collection RAN and the fact was absent. redacted: collection obtained the value and policy suppressed it. ⚠️ Each state is here because a fixture produces it; a state nothing can distinguish must not be declared (#121, #127).

reason.description: Required on every state. 'We did not observe this' and 'this was not observable' license different conclusions, and the state alone does not carry which one happened here.

allOf.$comment: A controller-managed run must name its tier and its boundary. Nested inside allOf per #82.

then.$comment: The controller knows both, so a record it produced without them is a collector defect rather than an unknown.

else.$comment: ⚠️ A host run may NOT carry a sandboxTier. This is the load-bearing constraint of the whole reshape: it makes 'no isolation claim' structural rather than a convention someone remembers. Recording a tier here would grant containment the run never had, and #42's rungs would report a strength nothing earned.

outcome.description: What happened when it ran. ⚠️ NOT a verdict on the assertion — a successful run can refute a claim, and a failed run can support one. Which way it bears is `assertion.supportedBy` / `refutedBy` (#82's naming rule), not this field.

observedAt.description: When the observation was made. Load-bearing for #96's applicability filter, which is the only reason it is required on an experiment.

capture.description: The raw capture — commands, output, logs. #86 in force: this artifact does not re-model a transcript, it points at one.

supersededBy.description: A later evidence record that replaces this one — a re-run, or a corrected observation. Read by #96's applicability filter: superseded evidence is not applicable, which is how a stale record stops manufacturing a contradiction.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103) — the clear advisory case, declared rather than inferred.

x-crossCutting.description: #25: validation is cross-cutting, not a tenth stage. Evidence is therefore produced by validation whenever a load-bearing assertion needs it, and no stage in stages/ claims it. That is why there is no x-stage here, and why #90's agreement check passes with none.
